samples.scenario: Business Email Compromise via Compromised Vendor Email Account Requesting Invoice Payment
samples.technical_data: [Complex structure with keys: email_headers, email_body, smtp_transaction_log, vendor_account_activity_log, dns_whois_vendors_domain, network_traffic_logs, endpoint_detection_alerts]
indicators: Invoice email from trustedvendor@vendor-example.com with SPF pass but DKIM fail
New login to vendor email account from IP 198.51.100.27 in Asia
Email requests payment to new bank account not previously associated with vendor
Vendor domain vendor-example.com registered over 5 years ago but subdomain spoofed
Endpoint detection alerts on vendor system show suspicious PowerShell execution
Unusual outbound network connections from vendor email server to unknown IPs
Email body includes urgent payment instructions with slight grammatical errors
samples.detection_method: Validate SPF, DKIM, and DMARC results combined with vendor account login geolocation anomalies. Monitor vendor email accounts for endpoint threats and unusual outbound traffic. Verify bank account details with established vendor contacts before payment. Employ email gateway rules to flag urgent payment requests with mismatched cryptographic signatures.

samples.scenario: Business Email Compromise via Cloud Email Service Credential Phishing and MFA Fatigue Exploitation
samples.technical_data: [Complex structure with keys: email_headers, email_body, cloud_service_auth_logs, mfa_challenge_logs, phishing_email_samples, dns_whois_phishing_domain, security_event_correlations]
indicators: Phishing email mimicking cloudservice@trustedmail.com with link to phishing domain cl0udsecures.com
Multiple failed MFA push notifications followed by successful login from VPN IP 45.77.123.88
Cloud email service logs show session token issued after MFA bypass
DNS WHOIS data shows phishing domain registered 2 days ago with privacy protection
Email contains request for wire transfer with sense of urgency and executive signature
Security event logs indicate MFA fatigue detected but not blocked
Recipient mailbox forwarding rule created to external suspicious address
samples.detection_method: Detect phishing domains via DNS monitoring and block known phishing URLs. Correlate failed MFA attempts with eventual successful logins from suspicious IPs. Alert on new mailbox forwarding rules and unusual token issuance events. Educate users on MFA fatigue risks and implement adaptive authentication policies.

Insider user with privileged access created fake vendor domain payroll-services.com
Financial transaction logs show payments routed to new vendor accounts
Internal chat logs reveal suspicious communication about vendor setup
Endpoint logs detect unusual file creation on insider’s workstation
Email content includes detailed invoice mimicking legitimate vendor format
No signatures or DKIM records available for fake vendor domain
samples.detection_method: Monitor domain registrations for vendor-like names and correlate with internal privileged user activity. Analyze financial transaction patterns for new payees. Endpoint monitoring for anomalous file and process activity by insiders.
